sources.title: Liu et al. 2023, Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

followUp: Explain why a team might still use retrieval even when all their documents fit in the window.

transfer.scenario: Your manager says: 'The new model has a million-token window, so we can drop retrieval and send the whole wiki.' Respond.
rubric: quality degrades with long inputs|context rot
access control and freshness still needed

narration.text: Our assistant reads text as tokens, which can be whole words, parts of words, or single characters.
The context window is the set of documents the model was trained on, so a bigger window means it knows more.
Everything in a request counts toward the window: the instructions, the history, any documents, and the answer itself.
Our whole handbook fits inside the window, so the model will use every part of it equally well.
When I paste a policy into the prompt, the model can use it for that call but does not keep it afterwards.
Word counts are only rough, so I check token usage with the provider's counter for the model we call.

planted.misconception: The context window is the training data.
planted.whyWrong: The context window is per-call working memory: what the model can see while answering this request. Training data was learned into the weights beforehand and is not in the window.
acceptableCorrections: The context window is what the model can see during one call, not its training data.
One request can hold more text in a bigger window, but the model's knowledge stays the same.

planted.misconception: If it fits in the window, the model uses all of it equally.
planted.whyWrong: Accuracy and recall degrade as the input gets longer, and models tend to use information at the start and end of a long input more reliably than the middle.
acceptableCorrections: Fitting in the window doesn't mean the model will use every part well; quality drops with length and position.
We should send only the relevant parts, or test that long-context answers are accurate.
planted.exceptions: With a short handbook and good tests, sending all of it can work fine; the error is assuming equal use.
